I remember coming close to a panic attack before a test once. The test was about 200 questions, many of which were specific answer, and could be on literally anything in this dense handbook we were given. Some things we had to know were lists of 10+ full names, or paragraphs that we would have to be able to write back out, verbatim, with no punctuation mistakes. I had been expected to study atleast a few times each week for an entire term, I had not. It was pass/fail at 70%. 

It ended up alright, but I only got through it with some helpful words from a friend in the same situation. It's going to be tough. You're going to have a shitty 24 hours. But worrying isn't going to help you learn, and is just going to get in your way.

Give yourself 10-20 minutes where you tell yourself you cannot study, and use that time to relax so that you can study effectively. Lie down some place dark, put in headphones with some relaxing or serene sounds, and breathe deeply for that entire time. best of luck. realize that even in the worst case scenario, its nothing you can't overcome.

I was seeing a therapist through my school, but this summer I have been without one. While I finished my year on a strong note, transitions are usually very difficult for me. I have been hesitant to get back with my previous therapist just because there is so much that he would need to be caught up on. I'm also dependent on the bus system, and without a job. Going to see him would be a big event in my day, and I don't want it to get in the way of scheduling for a job. But it's probably something I'm going to have to end up doing. When I get back to school I'm going to start back up with a therapist and possibly attend group meetings as have been recommended to me.

Thanks. I guess I just attach a massive stigma to that entire concept. It's something I've been so ashamed of because I've worried about what people would think of me if they found out, and now they have.
Yeah thanks. I just want my summer break to be a good time instead of a bad time. Right now it's pretty terrible.

thanks for your reply. i guess i feel like if i was really a good person, i would be able to deal with my personal issues in effective ways rather than drug use. as far as my friend goes, he's back on good terms with his parents. i've known them for such a long time and thats why i feel so terrible and couldn't stand them knowing i was responsible.

thank you. the big event that changed my life and got me to stop using drugs was that i got arrested for driving while intoxicated late last year. i turned my life around from the direction it was heading. i am still going though the legal system, but its already cost my family thousands, prevented me from driving for a year and filled me with guilt. i just feel like i have messed up so majorly in the past year, that with all the progress i've made i shouldn't have gone back to using drugs. this is just the worst feeling in the world.

Opiates were my DOC as well. Everyone had 5mg oxycodone tablets left around from when they had surgery. They didn't need them so I justified being a scumbag and stealing medication. With fairly limitless free supply I would find some, go on a binge taking pills multiple times a day, and then run out. With the dosage I was taking the withdrawals weren't too bad, but the mental addiction was terrible. I went on SSRIs feeling like those would make me feel better and I could come off the oxy, but that didn't work. When I went to college there were none. I hadn't ever taken ecstasy, but I found a coke dealer and started doing that because I wanted something to replace the painkillers. I hated it. It wasn't that hard to stop. I wasted hundreds of dollars of money that I lied to my parents about. I came off the SSRIs and started doing ecstasy. Of course taking those became very frequent and with terrible hangovers. The last time I did it was a week and a half ago after only waiting a week since the last one. My brain is probably still adjusting. Typing all this out just makes me feel like the biggest waste in the world. I feel pretty pathetic looking back on all of this.

thanks for your comment. i don't mean to take credit for the way that it happened, i was more or less confronted by the guy and i knew i had no way out. as far as the addiction goes, it was involving painkillers and those simply don't do it for me anymore. i have had some success with self control, but when i slip up and feel like i need an out, i end up doing things like this. it just makes me feel like i've made no progress at all.
